import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_2.csv"

# Step 1: Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # user_id, gender, age, occupation, zip
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # movie_id, title, genres
df_source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # user_id, movie_id, rating, timestamp

# Step 2: Analyze schemas and plan joins
# Target schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Source0 has user demographic info: user_id, gender, age, occupation, zip
# Source1 has movie info: movie_id, title, genres
# Source2 has user-movie rating info: user_id, movie_id, rating, timestamp

# We need to join all three sources to get all target columns:
# Join Source2 with Source0 on user_id to get age and occupation
# Join the result with Source1 on movie_id to get title

# Step 3: Perform joins

# Join Source2 and Source0 on 'user_id'
df_join_0_2 = pd.merge(df_source2, df_source0[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='left')

# Join the above result with Source1 on 'movie_id'
df_final = pd.merge(df_join_0_2, df_source1[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='left')

# Step 4: Select and reorder columns to match target schema
# Target schema order: title (string), user_id (float), movie_id (int), rating (float), timestamp (float), age (float), occupation (float)

# Convert types to match target schema explicitly
df_final['title'] = df_final['title'].astype(str)
df_final['user_id'] = df_final['user_id'].astype(float)
df_final['movie_id'] = df_final['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_final['rating'] = df_final['rating'].astype(float)
df_final['timestamp'] = df_final['timestamp'].astype(float)
df_final['age'] = df_final['age'].astype(float)
df_final['occupation'] = df_final['occupation'].astype(float)

df_target = df_final[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Step 5: Save the transformed data to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_18_2 with Source3_18_0 on user_id
join_1 = pd.merge(source2, source0, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_18_1 on movie_id
join_2 = pd.merge(join_1, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by title, user_id, movie_id (leftmost non-float unique columns in target)
# Aggregate rating, timestamp, age, occupation by mean
result = join_2.groupby(
    ["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False
).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Ensure columns order and types match target schema
result = result[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
